evidence.quote: pitryeṣu vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitān vettha nihitān parāke / medasaḥ kulyā upa tān sravantu satyā eṣām āśiṣaḥ santu kāmāḥ svāhā svadheti vapāyās trir juhoti
vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitān vettha nihitān parāke / medasaḥ kulyā upa tān sravantu satyā eṣām āśiṣaḥ santu kāmāḥ svāhā svadheti vapāyās trir juhoti

madhyamāyāṃ māghyā varṣe ca mahāvyāhṛtayaś catasro juhoti ye tātṛṣuḥ iti catasro'nudrutya vapāṃ juhuyāt / vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatrainān vettha sukṛtasya loke / medasaḥ kulyā upasrutās sravanti satyās santu yajamānasya kāmās svāhā / iti mahāvyāhṛtibhiś catasṛbhiḥ ye tātṛṣuḥ iti catasṛbhir aṣṭāv āhutīḥ sthālīpāko 'vadānamiśraḥ

verdict_reason: All three loci (KausS 5.9.14, KausS 11.5.1, KausGS 3.15.4) carry `pitrbhyo` inside the quoted mantra `vaha vapam jatavedah pitrbhyo ...`, closed by `iti`. The recipient is stated by the mantra, not by the ritual text.

evidence.quote: ādityāya vā eṣa prātarāhutyā mahāvratam upākaroti tat prāṇaḥ pratigṛṇāty annam annam ity ādityena hāsyāhnā mahāvrataṃ śastam bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti

verdict_reason: AB 5.28.9 `tat pranah pratigrnaty annam annam iti`: `annam annam` is the response formula the breath utters, not food offered to the Adityas.

evidence.quote: ādityāś ca ha vā aṅgirasaś cāspardhanta / vayaṃ pūrve svargaṃ lokam eṣyāma ity ādityā vayam ity aṅgirasaḥ / te 'ṅgirasa ādityebhyaḥ procuḥ / śvaḥ sutyā no yājayata na iti / teṣāṃ hāgnir dūta āsa / ta ādityā ūcuḥ / yadi vā ete pūrve yakṣyanty ete pūrve svargaṃ lokaṃ gamiṣyanti / abhi no 'surā bhaviṣyanti / upa taṃ yajñakratuṃ jānīma yena vayaṃ pūrve yajemahīti / ta etaṃ sādyaḥkraṃ yajñakratum apaśyan / teneṣṭvā pūrve svargaṃ lokam āyan / tena svargakāmo yajeta
evidence.translation: The Ādityas and the Aṅgirasas contended: 'We shall first reach the world of heaven' (said) the Ādityas, 'We shall' (said) the Aṅgirasas. The Aṅgirasas announced to the Ādityas: 'We possess a rite (at which the sacrifice of Soma takes place) on the next day (after the introductory days). So perform ye the sacrifice for us (as our offering priests). Of them Agni was the messenger. The Ādityas now said: 'If these Aṅgirasas, now, shall be the first to sacrifice, they shall reach the world of heaven first. Let us devise that rite by which we shall sacrifice first'. They beheld that one day-rite called sādyaḥkra (a soma-sacrifice at which the buying of the Soma and the other preliminary rites take place on the day of the soma feast itself). By performing it they went first to the world of heaven. He who wishes to reach the world of heaven should perform this rite.

verdict_reason: SankhSS 14.40.1 is the Adityas-and-Angirases narrative. No offering is prescribed to the Adityas in it.

evidence.quote: vṛṣṇe bṛhate svarvide agnaye śulkaṃ harāmi tviṣīmate sa na sthirān balavataḥ kṛṇotu jyok ca no jīvātave dadhāti agnaye svāhā ityuttarapūrvārdha āgneyam ājyabhāgaṃ juhoti

verdict_reason: KausS 1.4.1: both occurrences of `agnaye` sit inside the quoted mantra, closed by `ity`. The sutra's own words are `agneyam ajyabhagam juhoti` -- an adjective, not a dative. Under the contract that the DATIVE is the statement of recipiency this row has no dative belonging to the ritual text, so it is refused rather than re-justified on a different basis.

evidence.quote: ghnanti vā etat somaṃ yad abhiṣuṇvanti tasyaitām anustaraṇīṃ kurvanti yat saumyaḥ pitṛbhyo vā anustaraṇī tasmāt saumyasya pitṛmatyā yajati

verdict_reason: AB 3.32.2 is a Brahmana identification about the anustarani cow (`saumyah pitrbhyo va anustarani`). It does not state that the Fathers receive soma.

evidence.quote: imā rudrāya tavase kapardina iti pratyṛcaṃ gāvedhukaṃ caruṃ juhuyāt
evidence.translation: Let him offer boiled rice-grains with Gavedhuka-grass with (the hymn), 'These (prayers) to Rudra, the strong one, with braided hair' (Rig-veda I, 114), verse by verse.

verdict_reason: SankhGS 5.6.2 `ima rudraya tavase kapardina iti pratyrcam gavedhukam carum juhuyat`: the dative is inside the pratika, closed by `iti`.

evidence.quote: upākṛte vepamāne / yasmād bhīṣāvepiṣṭhās tato no 'bhayaṃ kuru / paśūn naḥ sarvān gopāya namo rudrāya mīḍhuṣe // svāheti juhoti
evidence.translation: When the victim after being brought up (to the sacrificial post) shivers, he performs a libation (of clarified butter in the Āhāvaniya) with (the verse): “From fear of what thou hast shivered, from that give us security; guard all our cattle. Homage to Rudra the bountiful”.

verdict_reason: SankhSS 13.2.2 `pasun nah sarvan gopaya namo rudraya midhuse`: the cattle are what Rudra is asked to PROTECT. Reading `pasu` beside a Rudra dative as an offering inverts the sentence.
